fanoutqa_019766.x:
Ron Weasley :: Characterisation :: Appearance and personality :: chunk_0010
In the first novel, Ron is described as tall, thin and gangling, with freckles, a long nose, and large hands and feet.[[43]](#cite_note-45) He has the trademark red hair of the Weasleys, and according to Rowling he has blue eyes.[[44]](#cite_note-46) Ron is known for his humour, loyalty, readiness to defend his friends, and his love of food. Rowling has described him as funny but insensitive.[[45]](#cite_note-47)[[46]](#cite_note-:1-48) She said that although he is the most immature of the three main characters, he matures in the final novel and acknowledges his weaknesses, which turns him into a man.[[46]](#cite_note-:1-48)

The entertainment website *[IGN](/wiki/IGN "IGN")* selected Ron as the third best *Harry Potter* character, writing that his status as comic relief makes him instantly endearing. The *IGN* writers claimed that unlike most sidekicks, Ron is not a coward or a simpleton, and is not content to "live in Harry's shadow". They said that he overcomes his shortcomings with "faithfulness and perseverance".[[47]](#cite_note-IGN_Top-49) *[Empire](/wiki/Empire_(magazine) "Empire (magazine)")* magazine included Ron's friendship with Harry as one of the 33 best friendships in film.[[48]](#cite_note-50)

In 2003, the British charity organisation [Comic Relief](/wiki/Comic_Relief "Comic Relief") performed a spoof story called *Harry Potter and the Secret Chamberpot of Azerbaijan*, in which [Jennifer Saunders](/wiki/Jennifer_Saunders "Jennifer Saunders") appeared as both Ron and J. K. Rowling.[[49]](#cite_note-51)[[50]](#cite_note-52)

Main articles: [Geography of Nepal](/wiki/Geography_of_Nepal "Geography of Nepal") and [Geology of Nepal](/wiki/Geology_of_Nepal "Geology of Nepal")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Nepal_topo_en.jpg/250px-Nepal_topo_en.jpg)](/wiki/File:Nepal_topo_en.jpg)

A topographic map of Nepal

Nepal is of roughly trapezoidal shape, about 800 kilometres (500 mi) long and 200 kilometres (120 mi) wide, with an area of 147,516 km2 (56,956 mi2). It lies between latitudes [26°](/wiki/26th_parallel_north "26th parallel north") and [31°N](/wiki/31st_parallel_north "31st parallel north"), and longitudes [80°](/wiki/80th_meridian_east "80th meridian east") and [89°E](/wiki/89th_meridian_east "89th meridian east"). Nepal's defining geological processes began 75 million years ago when the Indian plate, then part of the southern supercontinent [Gondwana](/wiki/Gondwana "Gondwana"), began a north-eastward [drift](/wiki/Plate_tectonics "Plate tectonics") caused by [seafloor spreading](/wiki/Seafloor_spreading "Seafloor spreading") to its south-west, and later, south and south-east.[[89]](#cite_note-ali-95) Simultaneously, the vast [Tethyn](/wiki/Tethys_Ocean "Tethys Ocean") [oceanic crust](/wiki/Oceanic_crust "Oceanic crust"), to its northeast, began to [subduct](/wiki/Subduction "Subduction") under the [Eurasian Plate](/wiki/Eurasian_Plate "Eurasian Plate").[[89]](#cite_note-ali-95) These dual processes, driven by convection in the Earth's [mantle](/wiki/Mantle_(geology) "Mantle (geology)"), both created the [Indian Ocean](/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean") and caused the Indian [continental crust](/wiki/Continental_crust "Continental crust") eventually to under-thrust Eurasia and to uplift the [Himalayas](/wiki/Himalayas "Himalayas").[[89]](#cite_note-ali-95)

Arsenal's tally of 13 League Championships is the [third highest](/wiki/List_of_English_football_champions#Total_titles_won "List of English football champions") in English football, after Liverpool (20) and Manchester United (20),[[240]](#cite_note-:8-245) and they were the first club [to reach](/wiki/List_of_English_football_champions#Football_League_First_Division_(1892–1992) "List of English football champions") a seventh and an eighth League Championship. As of June 2020, they are one of seven teams, the others being Manchester United, [Blackburn Rovers](/wiki/Blackburn_Rovers_F.C. "Blackburn Rovers F.C."), [Chelsea](/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") and Liverpool, to have won the Premier League since its formation in 1992.[[240]](#cite_note-:8-245)

[Boston Celtics](/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") general manager [Danny Ainge](/wiki/Danny_Ainge "Danny Ainge") traded the team's [No. 1 overall pick](/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") in the [2017 NBA draft](/wiki/2017_NBA_draft "2017 NBA draft") to the [Philadelphia 76ers](/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") for the third overall pick, which the Celtics used to select Jayson Tatum. Tatum was the Celtics' second consecutive No. 3 pick for a small forward, following [Jaylen Brown](/wiki/Jaylen_Brown "Jaylen Brown") in 2016, whom Tatum formed a [duo](/wiki/Jays_(Boston_Celtics) "Jays (Boston Celtics)") with.[[44]](#cite_note-44) During the [2017 NBA Summer League](/wiki/2017_NBA_Summer_League "2017 NBA Summer League") event in Utah, Tatum averaged 18.7 points, 9.7 rebounds, 2.3 steals, and 2.0 assists in nearly 33 minutes of action. Later, in Las Vegas, Tatum produced similar results, averaging 17.7 points, 8.0 rebounds, 1.0 assists, and 0.8 blocks in nearly 32 minutes of action in three games. Tatum was named to the All-Summer League Second Team alongside [Bryn Forbes](/wiki/Bryn_Forbes "Bryn Forbes"), [Cheick Diallo](/wiki/Cheick_Diallo "Cheick Diallo"), [Wayne Selden Jr.](/wiki/Wayne_Selden_Jr. "Wayne Selden Jr."), and [Kyle Kuzma](/wiki/Kyle_Kuzma "Kyle Kuzma").[[45]](#cite_note-45)

Belo Monte Dam :: Economics :: chunk_0012
The dam complex is expected to cost upwards of $16 billion and the transmission lines $2.5 billion. The project is being developed by the state-owned power company [Eletronorte](/wiki/Eletronorte "Eletronorte"), and would be funded largely by the [Brazilian Development Bank](/wiki/Brazilian_Development_Bank "Brazilian Development Bank") (BNDES).[[63]](#cite_note-aw-63) The project will also include substantial amounts of funding from Brazilian pension funds Petros, Previ, and Funcef. Private investors interested in the project include mining giants [Alcoa](/wiki/Alcoa "Alcoa") and [Vale](/wiki/Vale_do_Rio_Doce "Vale do Rio Doce") (to power new mines nearby like the proposed [Belo Sun](/w/index.php?title=Belo_Sun&action=edit&redlink=1 "Belo Sun (page does not exist)") gold mine[[51]](#cite_note-Watts2019-51)), construction conglomerates [Andrade Gutierrez](/wiki/Andrade_Gutierrez "Andrade Gutierrez"), Votorantim, Grupo OAS, Queiroz Galvão, Odebrecht and [Camargo Corrêa](/wiki/Camargo_Corr%C3%AAa "Camargo Corrêa"), and energy companies [GDF Suez](/wiki/GDF_Suez "GDF Suez") and Neoenergia.

In 2006, Conservation Strategy Fund (CSF) analyzed different cost-benefit scenarios for Belo Monte as an energy project, excluding environmental costs. Initial benefits appeared marginal. When simulating energy benefits using a modeling system it became obvious that Belo Monte would require additional upstream dams to provide water storage for dry season generation. [Abdominal ultrasonography](/wiki/Abdominal_ultrasonography "Abdominal ultrasonography") of pancreatic cancer (presumably adenocarcinoma), with a dilated [pancreatic duct](/wiki/Pancreatic_duct "Pancreatic duct") to the right.

The symptoms of pancreatic adenocarcinoma do not usually appear in the disease's early stages, and they are not individually distinctive to the disease.[[3]](#cite_note-Wolfgang2013-3)[[12]](#cite_note-Bond-Smith-12)[[39]](#cite_note-Cruz-39) The symptoms at diagnosis vary according to the location of the cancer in the pancreas, which anatomists divide (from left to right on most diagrams) into the thick head, the neck, and the tapering body, ending in the tail.

Regardless of a tumor's location, the most common symptom is unexplained weight loss, which may be considerable. A large minority (between 35% and 47%) of people diagnosed with the disease will have had nausea, vomiting, or a feeling of weakness. In early 2016, [Obama administration](/wiki/Presidency_of_Barack_Obama "Presidency of Barack Obama") officials vetted Jackson as a potential nominee to the [Supreme Court of the United States](/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") to fill the vacancy left by the death of Justice [Antonin Scalia](/wiki/Antonin_Scalia "Antonin Scalia").[[93]](#cite_note-93)[[94]](#cite_note-94)[[95]](#cite_note-95) Jackson was one of five candidates interviewed as a potential nominee.[[96]](#cite_note-96)

In early 2022, news outlets speculated that Biden would nominate Jackson to the United States Supreme Court to fill the seat vacated by Justice Breyer.[[97]](#cite_note-kapur-97)[[98]](#cite_note-98) Biden pledged during the [2020 United States presidential election](/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election "2020 United States presidential election") campaign to appoint a Black woman to the court should a vacancy occur.[[97]](#cite_note-kapur-97) Jackson
